facts.fact: A BMJ Open study (Seeiso and Mhlongo) states that the eRegister, piloted in 2018 at four health centres and two hospitals, is configured to compile facility-level data automatically and send it into the district health information management system; it gives no date or count of facilities doing so, so the document's published date is used.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health with implementing partners; ICAP funds computers, internet and support
systems.tiers: piloted in 2018 at four health centres and two hospitals, towards a rollout across 178 government facilities; study sites were a health centre, a filter clinic and a district hospital
receives facility-level data compiled by the eRegister

note: The eRegister is classed tracker because the study says it currently captures five programmes (elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis, tuberculosis, pregnancy and antenatal care, HIV and HPV, cervical cancer), though it also names a patient consultation module and pharmacy stock ordering, and says the government intends paper recording to be phased out once it is fully operational nationwide; so no EMR fact is recorded. Staff interviewed between December 2023 and March 2024 kept paper records alongside it, and its hardware and connectivity were donor-funded.
